summary: This tutorial covers using snippets in the Gedit text editor on Ubuntu Linux 14.04. Snippets are predefined code lines that help reduce repetitive typing. To enable snippets in Gedit, go to Edit > Preferences, select the Plugins tab, scroll down, and check the Snippets box. Writing a C program, you can use snippets by typing 'if' followed by Tab, which automatically inserts the if statement structure. The Intelligent Text Completion plugin also closes brackets and quotes automatically. To manage snippets, go to Tools > Manage Snippets, where you can view and create new ones. For example, clicking on "if" shows the syntax for an if statement. Creating your own snippet involves going to Tools > Manage Snippets, selecting C, clicking the plus icon, naming it (e.g., "helloworld"), editing the panel, and entering the desired code. This tutorial demonstrates how to efficiently write code using pre-defined snippets in Gedit.
